responsibility: Is the main implementation file for the 32-bit Arm backend. It owns most target hooks and backend policy for code generation, including CPU/architecture and ABI option processing, function/frame layout, prologue and epilogue emission, addressing-mode and constant legitimization, register classes and reload preferences, assembly printing, TLS/PIC and symbol handling, builtin and attribute support, cost and scheduling adjustments, minipool/literal-pool management, peephole and reorg helpers, far-branch generation, object-attribute emission, and target selftests over the generated Arm CPU/FPU data tables.
same_name_distinction: Provides the executable C implementation for the Arm port’s target hooks and backend policies, whereas the other same-stem files serve declarative or interface roles: arm.h supplies target macros and declarations, arm.md defines RTL instruction patterns and attributes, and arm.opt defines command-line option records and target variables.
